title: Prompt-and-output-shape-guarantees-for-locked-model-versions
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Define and implement a backward-compatibility contract for "locked" (pinned) model versions covering: prompt format invariants, output shape/schema guarantees, and model-parameter semantics (temperature, top_p, stop sequences, max_new_tokens). This ticket establishes the compatibility levels, enforcement mechanisms, and the publishing surface for the model's performance profile so downstream services can safely pin to a version with well-defined expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility levels documented: STRONG, SOFT, BEST_EFFORT with clear examples
API and model metadata extended to include 'compatibility_level' and 'compatibility_fingerprint' for each pinned model version
Automated regression harness added to onboarding pipeline that checks prompt->output shape invariants and parameter semantics against a canonical test-suite
Performance profile (p50/p95 latency, throughput tokens/s, memory/kv-cache footprint) published to model catalog for every pinned release
Console shows compatibility warnings when a rollout changes a model variant that downgrades compatibility level
Unit and integration tests added; failing tests block model publish in CI
decisions: Adopt a three-tier compatibility taxonomy: STRONG (no breaking changes to prompt schema or required parameters), SOFT (non-breaking additions allowed, backwards-compatible output fields), BEST_EFFORT (no guarantees beyond reasonable tokenization stability)
Represent compatibility with an immutable 'compatibility_fingerprint' string generated from: canonical tokenizer version, output-schema hash, and declared parameter semantics
Enforce STRONG compatibility in the onboarding CI by running the canonical prompt-suite and comparing normalized output shapes using stable canonicalizers (JSON schema + type coercion rules)
Publish performance profiles as machine-readable JSON plus human-friendly summary in the Console and model catalog
Do not attempt to guarantee identical logits or token-level probabilities across model variants; only output shape and parameter semantics are contract-covered
implementation_steps: Schema: extend model-catalog metadata with fields: compatibility_level, compatibility_fingerprint, published_performance_profile_url
Onboarding CI: add a 'compatibility-check' stage that runs the canonical prompt-suite against the candidate model and compares output shapes and parameter behavior
Create the canonical prompt-suite (start with 120 prompts covering chat, completion, structured output, tool-calling placeholders)
Implement a normalization library that transforms model output into canonical form for shape-comparison (strip whitespace tokens, normalize number formats, canonicalize timestamps)
Add a lightweight 'param-semantic-check' harness: validate temperature/top_p special-cases (e.g., temperature=0 deterministic path), stop-sequence handling, and max_new_tokens truncation semantics
Model catalog API: return compatibility metadata in /models and /models/:version endpoints
Console: surface a compatibility badge and link to the published performance profile
Add gating rule in publisher CI: downgrade to In Review if compatibility_fingerprint changes without documented migration notes
regression_tests: Prompt-suite baseline assertions: output JSON schema matches expected keys and types for each canonical prompt
Parameter invariants: setting temperature=0 yields deterministic canonicalized outputs for the canonical prompts
Stop-sequence semantics: sequences are honored regardless of tokenization boundary edge-cases (tests include sub-token splits)
Max_new_tokens: generated sequences must not exceed requested new tokens and must signal truncation consistently
Streaming vs. non-streaming: final canonicalized output must match between streaming and batch endpoints
monitoring_signals: Post-deploy drift alerts if output-shape failure rate > 0.5% on production traffic for pinned versions
Per-route regression metrics in Console: schema-violation-rate, param-behavior-delta, p50/p95 latency deltas vs published profile
Automated consumer breakage report emailed to owning team if a pinned version's compatibility_level changes
A/B safety checks for rollouts: baseline compatibility health must be green before >20% traffic shift
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Design + API changes (2 sprints) — metadata schema and catalog endpoints only
Phase 2: CI harness + canonical prompt-suite (1 sprint) — block model publishes that fail STRONG checks
Phase 3: Console + alerts (1 sprint) — surface badges and runbook links
Phase 4: Retro & customer comms (1 sprint) — notify pilot customers and gather feedback
Fallback: when an incompatible change is detected during a release, automatically revert the model alias to previous pinned_version and open emergency rollback runbook
discussion_notes: PM concern: some enterprise customers treat pinned versions as SLAs — recommended we offer 'compatibility SLA' as part of Dedicated contracts
Design note: show compatibility_level as color-coded badge (green/yellow/red) and provide a tool-tip that explains the three levels
Eng tradeoff: canonicalization cannot be perfect; we will accept a small class of normalization heuristics (numbers, timestamps) but log normalized diffs to aid debugging
Security: compatibility_fingerprint must be deterministic and collision-resistant; we will use SHA256 over canonicalized metadata string
next_steps: Schedule 1-hour design review with PM and Design to finalize badge copy (owner: Diego Moreno)
Add the initial 120 canonical prompts to the onboarding repo and mark them as experimental
Create the first compatibility_fingerprint generator RFC and submit to ARCH board
